name: Andrew Fentress
current_role: Chairman of the Board and Managing Director, Capital Markets (principal executive officer), ACRES Commercial Realty Corp. (NYSE: ACR); co-founder, ACRES Capital
profile: Commercial real estate lender who co-founded ACRES Capital in 2012 and has chaired mortgage REIT ACRES Commercial Realty since July 2020. He started at Morgan Stanley in institutional equities in 1995, moved into private credit in 2004 and was a founding/managing partner of direct lender Medley before ACRES, which he says manages about $4B.
interesting_fact: He pivoted from corporate private credit to commercial real estate lending after the financial crisis, building ACRES on a loss-control philosophy: 'In credit, you're only as good as your losses.'
deep_cut_fact: He sailed four years on Boston College's varsity sailing team, competing in national championships, and right after college sold NordicTrack fitness equipment for an entrepreneur he had worked for as a student, before Morgan Stanley.
notes: Appeared on Dakota Rainmaker podcast (comfortable with podcast format). Internalization of ACR management closed Aug 2026 per secondary profile; title may be evolving.

name: David S. Graziosi
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, Allison Transmission Holdings Inc. (NYSE: ALSN)
profile: Indianapolis-based industrial executive who has led Allison Transmission, the maker of commercial and defense vehicle automatic transmissions, as CEO since June 2018 and chair since about 2021. He joined in November 2007 as EVP, CFO and treasurer, just after GM sold Allison to Carlyle and Onex, and became president in 2016. Earlier he was CFO at Berry Plastics and Covalence Specialty Adhesives (per secondary profile).
interesting_fact: He joined Allison right after GM's 2007 carve-out sale to Carlyle and Onex, helped take it public in 2012, and as CEO has steered it into electrified propulsion and defense (e.g. 2026 deal to supply transmissions for BAE Systems Hagglunds CV90 MkIV vehicles).
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a tax auditor before moving into finance roles at multinational manufacturers.
notes: Low personal media profile; route via Allison media relations (Sjoerd Vos, Global Brand + External Communications, listed on 2026 releases). IPO 2012 detail is general company history.

name: James D Dee
current_role: Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, Carpenter Technology Corporation (NYSE: CRS)
profile: Corporate lawyer who has been Carpenter Technology's top legal officer since September 2010 (SVP since August 2020). Carpenter, based in Reading, PA, makes specialty alloys for aerospace, defense, energy and medical markets. Before Carpenter he was a VP/General Counsel and Secretary at SPS Technologies and later C&D Technologies (battery/power systems). His wealth stems from long-held CRS equity awards.
interesting_fact: He has been general counsel through Carpenter's transformation into a high-margin aerospace and defense alloy supplier, a period in which CRS shares rose many-fold; he also sits on the boards of Carpenter's European and UK subsidiaries.
deep_cut_fact: Before Carpenter he spent years as general counsel of SPS Technologies, a Jenkintown, PA aerospace fastener maker, and then served as Chief Administrative Officer at C&D Technologies, an industrial battery company (per aggregator profiles; verify against proxy filings).
notes: Non-founder executive with minimal public profile; career details come from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener, Fintool) and dates conflict slightly. Approach via Carpenter IR/communications.

name: Kevin Hochman
current_role: President and CEO, Brinker International (NYSE: EAT), and President of Chili's Grill & Bar
profile: Consumer-brand marketer turned restaurant CEO who has run Brinker since June 2022, leading a Chili's turnaround that lifted market cap from about $1.3B to over $7B. Previously spent 18 years at Procter & Gamble and 2014-2022 at Yum! Brands, as KFC U.S. CMO then president, also running Pizza Hut U.S. from 2020-22.
interesting_fact: As KFC's CMO he created the rotating-celebrity Colonel Sanders campaign and was named Forbes' No. 2 most influential CMO in the world; at Chili's he was named Restaurant Business Restaurant Leader of the Year for the turnaround.
deep_cut_fact: At P&G he worked on the famous Old Spice turnaround campaign and was North America Cosmetics Business Leader; he holds dual Penn degrees (Wharton BS economics and Annenberg BA communication) and lists running, golf, tennis and cooking as hobbies.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who frequently speaks at conferences and on business podcasts; Brinker media relations is the best route.

name: Vikas Sinha
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Scholar Rock Holding Corp. (Nasdaq: SRRK); board member and audit chair, ElevateBio
profile: Veteran biotech CFO who spent 11 years as CFO of Alexion Pharmaceuticals, where market cap grew from about $600M to over $30B and revenue from zero to $3B+. He co-founded cell/gene-therapy company ElevateBio, was president and CFO of AlloVir (2018-2025), and became Scholar Rock CFO in April 2025. He was also a Verona Pharma director until Merck acquired it in 2025.
interesting_fact: He helped take Alexion from a pre-revenue rare-disease company to a $30B+ market cap; Alexion was later acquired by AstraZeneca for about $39B.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he spent years at Bayer in the U.S., Japan, Germany and Canada, including as CFO of Bayer Yakuhin in Japan; he earned his MBA at the Asian Institute of Management in Manila and is both an Indian Chartered Accountant and a U.S. CPA.
notes: Low-profile finance executive; Scholar Rock IR/media is the official route. Verona Pharma directorship ended with Merck acquisition (2025); AstraZeneca deal value is general public knowledge.

name: Roderick A. Larson
current_role: President and CEO, Oceaneering International (NYSE: OII); director, NPK International
profile: Engineer-turned-CEO who has led Houston-based Oceaneering, a subsea robotics/ROV and offshore energy services company, since May 2017 after joining as COO in 2012. He spent about 22 years at Baker Hughes (starting in wireline at Western Atlas), working deepwater Gulf of Mexico operations and rising to president of Latin America. North Dakota State University electrical engineering grad with a Rice MBA.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Oceaneering applies its subsea robotics know-how far beyond oil and gas, building autonomous vehicles for factories, aerospace work and trackless ride systems for theme parks.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up on a North Dakota farm and started out running electric downhole surveys from the back of a wireline truck, which he described as 'a farm boy battling the elements'; he joked that after an oil-firm practice interview, 'The only way to mess it up was to go into the oil field.'
notes: Strong fit for energy podcast (offshore energy, robotics, energy transition). IR contact in 2026 releases is Hilary Frisbie, Senior Director IR.

name: Mark McKinney
current_role: Private investor; 5% holder of Cardinal Infrastructure Group (Nasdaq: CDNL); co-founder of Proficient Auto Logistics (Nasdaq: PAL)
profile: Roll-up specialist and investment manager. With partner Ross Berner he co-founded Proficient Auto Logistics, which combined auto-transport carriers and IPO'd in May 2024 (both stepped off the board at IPO). Both men also hold ~5% pre-IPO stakes in Raleigh-based civil/site-development contractor Cardinal Infrastructure Group, which IPO'd in Dec 2025. In the late 1990s they were co-chief acquisition officers of auto hauler United Road Services.
interesting_fact: He and Ross Berner have repeatedly used the same playbook: assemble fragmented industrial service companies and take them public at once, from United Road Services in the 1990s to Proficient Auto Logistics (2024) and, as investors, Cardinal Infrastructure (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In the late 1990s he was co-chief acquisition officer of United Road Services, the Michigan-based auto hauler that grew into the U.S. market leader with nearly 2,000 trucks.
notes: Identity link: same SEC filer (CIK 0001079404) filed Form 3s for both Proficient Auto Logistics (2024) and Cardinal (2025) plus a Feb 2026 13G; Cardinal proxy lists him at c/o Cardinal, Raleigh (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2079999/000119312526177393/cdnl-20260424.htm). Passive holder, not an officer; no public contacts found. Common name - verify before outreach.

name: James Finnigan
current_role: Reportedly President & Creator, Bernie's Best (Austin-based dog supplement brand, maker of 'Perfect Poop'); SoFi co-founder (unverified current role, per directory profiles)
profile: One of four Stanford GSB students (with Mike Cagney, Dan Macklin and Ian Brady) who founded SoFi in 2011 as an alumni-funded student-loan refinancer; SoFi later became a Nasdaq-listed digital bank. He came to Stanford with an engineering and consulting background and worked on SoFi product, finance and legal. Directory profiles say that since Dec 2018 he has run Bernie's Best, a dog-supplement company.
interesting_fact: SoFi began as a Stanford GSB class-adjacent project in which alumni funded loans for current students; Finnigan said they saw 'a huge market, a huge problem, and ripe for change.'
deep_cut_fact: During SoFi's research phase he personally phoned nearly two dozen university financial-aid directors, noting that as a student they got through: 'If we weren't in school and said we're calling from XYZ loan company, they'd be like, "Hold on."'
notes: Low public profile. Bernie's Best link comes only from Crunchbase/Coinpedia-type profiles (https://crunchbase.com/person/james-finnigan); the company site does not name him, and its contact page (help@bernies.com) is customer support. Verify before outreach; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Christopher K. Zarins
current_role: Co-founder, HeartFlow, Inc. (Nasdaq: HTFL); Professor Emeritus of Surgery, Stanford University
profile: Latvian-born vascular surgeon (b. 1943) who chaired vascular surgery at the University of Chicago and then Stanford, where he moved in 1993. In 2007 he co-founded HeartFlow with biomedical engineer Charles Taylor to turn coronary CT scans into non-invasive blood-flow (FFR-CT) models; he left full-time faculty in 2010 to focus on the company, now Nasdaq-listed.
interesting_fact: HeartFlow was the first company to come out of Fogarty Innovation, and its FFR-CT technology uses computational fluid dynamics to tell doctors whether a coronary blockage actually restricts blood flow, without a catheter.
deep_cut_fact: With his siblings he founded the Honorary Foundation of Richard Zarins (2013), named for their Lutheran-pastor father, which has given $105,000+ to the University of Latvia for scholarships and books on 20th-century Latvian history; he fled Latvia as an infant in 1944 via Sweden.
notes: Age ~82; academic, publishes widely (350+ papers). Also on the board of the Latvian Medical Foundation. HeartFlow contacts are the company's named IR (Nick Laudico) and media (Elliot Levy) leads from Nov 2026 release. Bio: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Zarins

name: Patrick Sigrist
current_role: Co-founder of iFood (Brazil); current role not verified
profile: Brazilian entrepreneur who co-founded iFood in May 2011 with Eduardo Baer, Guilherme Bonifacio and Felipe Fioravante. iFood, backed by Movile/Prosus, became Latin America's dominant food-delivery app with over 80% of Brazil's meal-delivery market; Prosus bought Just Eat Takeaway's 33% stake for EUR1.8B in 2022.
interesting_fact: iFood started offline: its roots go back to Disk Cook (1997), a printed menu guide with a telephone call centre that took orders, which moved online and was rebranded iFood about 14 years later.
notes: Could not verify his current activity or personal channels (web-search budget exhausted mid-lane). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFood. Brazil-based; Portuguese-language outreach and LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Chen Hang
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Manycore Tech Inc. (Qunhe Keji), Hangzhou; listed in Hong Kong April 2026
profile: Chinese software entrepreneur who co-founded Manycore in 2011 with fellow University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign graduates Huang Xiaohuang and Zhu Hao. Its cloud-rendered Kujiale (international: Coohom) is, per Frost & Sullivan, the world's largest spatial-design platform by MAU. Backed by IDG, Hillhouse and Coatue, Manycore completed its HKEX IPO on 17 April 2026.
interesting_fact: Manycore is one of Hangzhou's 'Six Little Dragons' alongside DeepSeek, Unitree Robotics and Game Science (Black Myth: Wukong), and in Nov 2024 launched SpatialVerse, a spatial-intelligence platform for training AI in indoor 3D environments.
notes: Company facts from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manycore_Tech. Interesting for data-center angle: Kujiale relies on cloud GPU rendering. Chinese-language outreach via Manycore IR (HKEX filings) is likely the official route; no personal channels verified. Web search budget ran out before deep-cut research.

name: Abhijit Kane
current_role: Co-founder and Product Architect, Postman, Inc.
profile: Indian software engineer who co-founded Postman, the API development and testing platform used by tens of millions of developers, with Abhinav Asthana and Ankit Sobti. The app began in 2012 as Asthana's Chrome-store side project in Bangalore; Kane, a former colleague, joined to build Postman Inc., which moved HQ to San Francisco in 2017. He remains with the company as Product Architect.
interesting_fact: Postman reached 500,000 users with no marketing before the company was even formed; in March 2026 it relaunched as a Git-native, AI-native platform for the agentic era.
deep_cut_fact: Before Postman he was a software engineer at Adobe and Walmart, then at TeliportMe, Abhinav Asthana's first startup, where the team's struggle to share a complex API across the development cycle helped spark Postman. A BITS Pilani graduate, he is learning to play the piano.
notes: Lower-profile, engineering-focused co-founder; CEO Abhinav Asthana is the public face. info@postman.com is the general company address.

name: Kaisei Hamamoto
current_role: President and CEO (Representative Director), SmartNews, Inc.
profile: Japanese software engineer (b. 1981, Utsunomiya) who co-founded news-aggregation app SmartNews with Ken Suzuki in 2012 (originally Gocro). He was co-CEO, then COO and chief engineer from 2019, and became President & CEO in November 2023; since March 2025 he is the company's sole representative director. Forbes Japan ranked him Japan's No. 1 entrepreneur in 2020.
interesting_fact: SmartNews, built on his natural-language-processing background, grew into one of Japan's most-used news apps and expanded to the U.S.; he topped Forbes Japan's entrepreneur ranking in 2020 after placing second in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: At Tokyo Tech he sang in and conducted the mixed choir Chor Kleines, and he co-translated the Japanese editions of O'Reilly's 'Version Control with Subversion' (2009) and 'Version Control with Git' (2010); in 2009 he won the Yahoo! JAPAN Internet Creative Award grand prize.
notes: Japanese-language approach recommended. Blog listed as external link on his Japanese Wikipedia page (stub tagged as relying on primary sources). SmartNews leadership history: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B9%E3%83%9E%E3%83%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%8B%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B9

name: Visar Nimani
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Information Officer, Upgrade, Inc.
profile: Technology executive and co-founder of San Francisco neobank Upgrade, launched in 2016-17 by LendingClub founder Renaud Laplanche with former colleagues. As CIO he runs the systems behind Upgrade's personal loans, credit cards and banking products; the company, last valued around $7B, has raised about $750M in equity and helped customers access over $50B in credit.
interesting_fact: Upgrade's founding team largely came from LendingClub, the pioneer of U.S. marketplace lending, and rebuilt a consumer-credit platform from scratch that now serves millions of customers.

name: Arif Nathoo
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Komodo Health (San Francisco)
profile: Physician-turned-entrepreneur (MD) who co-founded healthcare data and analytics company Komodo Health with Web Sun. Komodo maps patient journeys from de-identified real-world healthcare data for life-sciences companies and was valued at about $3B. Nathoo oversees data science, engineering and product development and, as of 2026, shares the CEO role with Sun.
interesting_fact: Komodo's 'Healthcare Map' tracks de-identified patient encounters across the U.S. healthcare system, letting drug makers and payers see real-world treatment patterns rather than relying on trial data alone.
notes: Bio details (medical training, prior employers) not verified this pass; web-search budget exhausted. Co-CEO arrangement with Web Sun noted on the press page (June 2026). Komodo PR is also supported by agency Real Chemistry.

name: Nagarjuna Venna
current_role: Co-founder, BitSight Technologies (Boston); current role not verified
profile: Co-founder, with Stephen Boyer, of BitSight (2011), the Boston cybersecurity-ratings company that scores the security posture of 200,000+ organizations much as credit agencies rate debt. He served as an executive officer and director (per 2018 SEC Form D). BitSight later took a $250M investment from Moody's (2021) and acquired Cybersixgill (2024).
interesting_fact: BitSight pioneered outside-in 'security ratings': it rates companies' cyber risk from externally observable data, a model that drew Moody's as a $250M strategic investor.

name: Andrew Boni
current_role: Founder and Chief Scientist, Iterable (San Francisco)
profile: Software entrepreneur who co-founded customer-engagement/marketing-automation platform Iterable in 2013 with Justin (Haoran) Zhu. Iterable powers cross-channel messaging for consumer brands and was valued around $2B. Boni served as CEO from 2021 to 2025 and is now Founder and Chief Scientist as Iterable pushes into AI and agentic marketing.

name: Mada Seghete
current_role: Co-founder, Branch (Branch Metrics); no longer listed on Branch's leadership page; current role not verified
profile: Romanian-born entrepreneur (Madalina Seghete) who co-founded mobile deep-linking and attribution company Branch on 15 April 2014 with Alex Austin, Mike Molinet and Dmitri Gaskin. Branch went through Stanford's StartX accelerator, raised hundreds of millions (incl. a ~EUR270M round) and reached a ~$4B valuation; it later bought Nova Launcher.
interesting_fact: Branch began because its founders, building their own app, found that links to in-app content kept breaking, and asked 'Why hadn't anyone solved mobile linking?'; months later it won gold at the Mobile World Congress 2015 startup showdown.
